clips.title: The story
paras: At Ravenholdt Manor, Fahrad maintains an endless demand for sturdy, locked containers to train the guild's rising rogues. Because the practice locks provided by the manor's own craftsman are too simple for advanced students, Fahrad trades specialized throwing knives to anyone willing to supply authentic heavy junkboxes.

Within the hidden redoubt of Ravenholdt Manor, nestled in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, training never ceases. Master thief Fahrad oversees instruction for the guild's operatives, placing high value on practical lockpicking mastery. While Zan provides practice contraptions for new recruits, Fahrad considers that crude work entirely unfit for experienced operatives who must crack real, stubborn mechanisms in the field.

To keep the manor supplied with real-world mechanisms, Fahrad contracts out for heavy junkboxes swiped from dangerous targets across Azeroth. Though only skilled thieves can lift these boxes from marks in the wild, Fahrad does not restrict his business solely to rogues. Anyone who delivers batches of these locked chests—even if already picked clean of major valuables—earns Fahrad's favor and a supply of the manor's lethally balanced throwing blades, provided a token coin remains inside to motivate the initiates.

clips.title: Progress
paras: My rogues need to hone their lockpicking skills, and I need locks of adequate difficulty—the stuff Zan makes us is unfit for all but the lowliest neophytes.
Tell ya what, if you bring me 5 Heavy Junkboxes, I'll provide you with some of the finest throwing knives known to roguekind.
You can unlock the boxes and rifle through them, but you'll have to leave at least a few coins in them... Even a rogue in training needs motivation.

clips.title: Completion
paras: May these knives find a place in someone's heart.
